name: Поля, пастки й зв’язки
description:
In this lesson the same principle as in the previous two lessons, the difference being that here we focus on the pin.

In Example 1, white must cleverly attack a piece and indirectly a mating square.

In Example 2, white must cleverly attack a pinned piece. If white does not choose the right move, black escapes by counterattacking a checkmating square.

What do you have to do?

Win material by pinning or attacking a pinned piece. Be careful not to give the other player a chance to defend by counterattacking.

examples.text:
1.Rb1! pins the knight. If black moves the knight anyway, they are quickly mated: 1...Na2 2.Rb8+ Bc8 3.Rxc8+ Bd8 4.Rxd8#. However if the knight stays in its place then black loses material.

Clumsy is 1.Rb2 (red arrow). Black can remove the knight with check: 1...Nd3+! To make matters worse, this also costs White material: a knight fork!

1.Bf5! attacks the pinned knight. If Black removes the rook, White has time to take the knight: 1...Rb8 2.Rxd7 and now 2...Rb1+ fails to 3.Bxb1. Immediately it is clear why the bishop should be on the diagonal b1-h7!

1.Bc6 (red arrow) fails to 1...Rb8! (green arrow). Capturing the knight now is not a good idea, because then Black has 2...Rb1+ followed by 3...Rxd1#. If white makes luft, then black has time to save the knight.

texts: Exploit the white king's weakness. Keep calculating!
Exploit the weakness of the white king.
